_comment: Pinned regression contract for the generated merchant table.
This file is the gate. scripts/validate-merchant-table.mjs refuses to promote
a generated candidate that fails any case here, and tests/cases/34-merchant-table.test.js
runs the same cases against the table that is actually committed. A model
regenerating the table unattended can therefore widen coverage but cannot
silently regress a descriptor we already know the right answer for.
Every case below is a real failure mode observed in the pre-table parser,

cases.why: Over-collapse. The pre-table parser split on '*' and returned 'PAYPAL', so every PayPal-routed subscription merged into one fake merchant with a meaningless median amount.
Same bug, second victim. Proves the aggregator strip generalises rather than special-casing Spotify.
Under-collapse. The txn-id regex required a leading digit, so 'P34F9G8' survived. One subscription became N singletons, each dropped by the list.length < 2 guard -- a silent miss, the worst kind.

An unknown merchant behind a known aggregator. The aggregator is stripped, then the existing regex pass handles the remainder -- this pins that the fallback path stays wired and still returns uppercase.

_mustNotResolve_comment: Businesses that are NOT the brand hiding inside their name. These must fall
through to the regex pass untouched.
The first implementation matched patterns with a plain indexOf, so a short
pattern matched inside an unrelated word: 'NEST' hit THE HONEST COMPANY and
NESTLE, 'PLEX' hit COMPLEX / PLEXUS / DUPLEX, 'PHILO' hit PHILOSOPHY.
Each produced a confident WRONG merchant name -- the failure mode the
statement-parser header calls worse than no answer at all. Matching is now
whole-token. These cases exist so it stays that way, and so a regeneration
cannot add a pattern short enough to bring the problem back.
